en: The *Loṣṭha-dhāraṇī Sūtra* Spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Court Scattered Official, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments,
Great Master of Enlightened Teaching, Subject Faxian, by Imperial Decree.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying:
"Listen attentively; now I shall proclaim to you the lakṣa-dhāraṇī."
This dhāraṇī is difficult to encounter,
just as it is for the Buddhas to appear in the world.
Ānanda, if there are sentient beings who obtain this dhāraṇī and are able to receive and uphold it,
the merit obtained by such persons will be no different from that of upholding a hundred thousand buddhas (lakṣa).
It can cause all sentient beings to generate a great mass of merit and can extinguish the immeasurable heavy sins of sentient beings.
At that time, the World-Honored One then spoke this lakṣa-dhāraṇī:
Namaḥ samantabuddhānām | Oṃ namo bhagavate vipulajñānasaṃbhāropacitāya prabhāsakaratejomūrtaye tathāgatāya ||
Āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā | bodhi bodhi sarvatathāgatānucāriṇi dharadhara harahara pravaradvāre ||1||

Ānanda received it with joy and faith, prostrated, and withdrew.
The Sūtra on the Lo-cha Dhāraṇī Spoken by the Buddha.
